title: Order of the Court — regular bail
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 4471 of 2026. The petitioner, through counsel, seeks the grant of regular bail in a case registered under Sections 420, 467 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, at Police Station Sector 34, Chandigarh. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has already remained in custody for four months and eleven days, that the investigation stands concluded, and that the challan has been presented before the trial court on the fourteenth of July, 2026. It is further submitted that the recovery, if any, has already been effected, and that the petitioner is neither a previous convict nor involved in any other case of a like nature. The learned State counsel, on the other hand, opposes the prayer and contends that the allegations are grave, that the amount alleged to have been misappropriated is substantial, and that the petitioner, if released, is likely to influence the material witnesses who are yet to be examined. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the custody certificate placed on the record, this Court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose would be served by keeping the petitioner behind bars during the pendency of the trial, particularly when the challan already stands presented and the recovery is complete. However, the apprehension expressed by the State with regard to the witnesses cannot be brushed aside altogether. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed. The petitioner is ordered to be released on regular bail on his furnishing bail bonds and surety bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court, subject to the following conditions. First, the petitioner shall join the trial on each and every date of hearing, unless his personal presence is specifically exempted. Second, the petitioner shall not, directly or indirectly, tamper with the prosecution evidence or attempt to win over any of the witnesses. Third, the petitioner shall not leave the country without the prior permission of the trial court, and shall deposit his passport, if any, with that court. Fourth, in the event of the petitioner being found to have violated any of the conditions imposed herein, it shall be open to the prosecution to move an appropriate application for the cancellation of bail. It is made clear that nothing observed hereinabove shall be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case, and the observations made are confined to the disposal of the present bail application alone. The petition stands disposed of in the above terms. A copy of this order be sent to the trial court concerned for information and compliance. Ordered accordingly.

title: Office Memorandum — earned leave
body: Subject: Regulation of earned leave and the maintenance of the leave account in respect of the ministerial establishment. Reference: The instructions issued vide this office endorsement No. Estt-II/2026/1187, dated the second of March, 2026, and the rules framed thereunder. The undersigned is directed to invite the attention of all the branch officers and the officials of the ministerial establishment to the subject and the reference cited above, and to convey the following instructions for strict compliance. It has been observed that, in a number of cases, applications for the grant of earned leave are being submitted at the eleventh hour, and often after the leave has already been availed of, which practice is wholly irregular and contrary to the rules on the subject. All the officials are, therefore, informed that an application for earned leave must reach the office of the undersigned at least seven clear days before the date from which the leave is proposed to be availed, save in cases of genuine emergency, the nature of which shall be recorded in writing. The leave account of each official shall be maintained by the dealing hand in the prescribed register, and shall be reconciled at the close of every quarter. No leave shall be treated as sanctioned unless and until a formal order to that effect has been issued by the competent authority. The head of each branch shall ensure that, before forwarding any application, the balance at the credit of the official concerned is duly verified with reference to the entries in the service book. Where an official proceeds on leave without the prior sanction of the competent authority, the period of absence shall, subject to the orders of that authority, be liable to be treated as leave without pay, without prejudice to any disciplinary action that may be warranted. It is further clarified that the sanctioning authority may, in the interest of the public service, refuse, curtail or revoke the leave already sanctioned, and no official shall claim leave as a matter of right. The branch officers are requested to bring these instructions to the notice of every official working under their respective charge, and to obtain their dated signatures in token of having read and understood the same. A compliance report, in the enclosed proforma, shall be furnished to the establishment branch not later than the fifteenth of this month. This issues with the approval of the competent authority. All concerned are expected to adhere to these instructions in letter and in spirit, so that the disposal of the leave applications is regulated in an orderly and timely manner, and the leave accounts are kept up to date at all times.

title: Notice — publication of the daily cause list
body: Notice for the information of the members of the Bar and the general public. It is hereby notified that, with effect from the first working day of the coming month, the daily cause list of this Court shall be published on the official web portal by six o'clock in the evening on the preceding working day, and the practice of circulating printed copies in the branches shall be discontinued in a phased manner. The advocates appearing in the matters listed before the various benches are advised to consult the electronic cause list carefully, and to note the bench, the item number and the approximate time indicated against each case. The matters shall ordinarily be taken up in the serial order in which they appear in the list, subject to such adjustments as the bench concerned may find necessary in the course of the day. Where a matter has been shown as part-heard, it shall be listed at the top of the board of the bench before which it remained part-heard, and shall be taken up before the fresh matters are called out. In cases which are listed for the first time after notice, the counsel are requested to ensure that the process fee and the requisite number of copies have been filed well in advance, so that the issuance of notice is not delayed on account of any office objection. The office objections, if any, are displayed against the concerned items in the cause list itself, and it shall be the responsibility of the counsel to have such objections removed before the date of hearing. The urgent matters which are mentioned before the bench and are directed to be listed shall be included in an additional or supplementary cause list, which shall be published separately on the same portal. The members of the Bar are further informed that any discrepancy noticed in the cause list, whether in the description of the parties, the nature of the matter, or the stage at which it is shown, may be brought to the notice of the deputy registrar (judicial) in writing, so that the necessary correction is carried out at the earliest. The litigants who appear in person are advised to reach the Court well before the commencement of the day's proceedings, and to seek the assistance of the facilitation centre established in the main building for ascertaining the courtroom in which their matter has been listed. This arrangement is being introduced with a view to ensuring transparency, saving paper, and enabling the counsel and the litigants to plan their appearances in an informed manner. All concerned are requested to co-operate in the smooth implementation of this arrangement. Issued under the orders of the competent authority for general information.

title: Summons to the defendant
body: In the Court of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Chandigarh. Civil Suit No. 812 of 2026, titled as the plaintiff versus the defendant, for the recovery of a sum of money together with interest and costs. To the defendant, resident of House No. 219, Sector 21, Chandigarh. Whereas the plaintiff, named above, has instituted a suit against you for the recovery of the amount described in the plaint, a copy whereof is annexed to this summons, you are hereby summoned to appear before this Court, in person or through a duly instructed pleader, on the nineteenth of October, 2026, at ten o'clock in the forenoon, to answer the claim made against you. You are directed to file your written statement, along with the documents upon which you intend to rely in support of your defence, on or before the said date, and to bring with you, or to send by a pleader, all the documents and witnesses upon whose evidence you propose to rely in support of your case. Take notice that, in default of your appearance on the day and at the hour aforesaid, the suit shall be heard and determined in your absence, and an ex parte decree may be passed against you, which shall be binding upon you in all respects. You are further informed that, should you admit the claim of the plaintiff, either wholly or in part, you may deposit the admitted amount in this Court, and such deposit shall be taken into account at the time of the final adjudication of the suit. If you contend that the claim of the plaintiff is barred by limitation, or that this Court has no jurisdiction to try the suit, or that the plaint is liable to be rejected on any ground available in law, you shall raise such objection specifically in your written statement, and shall not be permitted to raise it at a later stage save with the leave of the Court. It is made clear that a mere denial of the averments contained in the plaint shall not be treated as a sufficient answer, and that you are required to deal specifically with each of the material allegations, admitting, denying or explaining the same, as the case may be. The plaintiff has valued the suit for the purposes of court fee and jurisdiction at the amount stated in the plaint, and the requisite court fee stands affixed thereon. Given under my hand and the seal of this Court, on this the seventh day of September, in the year two thousand and twenty-six. By order of the Court, the reader is directed to ensure due service of this summons upon the defendant in accordance with law.

title: Judgment — regular second appeal
body: This regular second appeal has been preferred by the defendant against the judgment and decree passed by the learned lower appellate court, whereby the appeal filed by the plaintiff was accepted, the judgment of the trial court was set aside, and the suit for possession by way of specific performance of the agreement to sell was decreed in favour of the plaintiff. The facts, in brief, are that the plaintiff instituted a suit for specific performance on the averment that the defendant had entered into an agreement to sell the suit property for a stated consideration, that a substantial part of the sale consideration was paid at the time of the execution of the agreement, and that the defendant, despite repeated requests and a legal notice, failed to execute the sale deed within the stipulated period. The defendant contested the suit and denied the execution of the agreement, and pleaded, in the alternative, that the plaintiff was never ready and willing to perform his part of the contract. The trial court, on an appreciation of the evidence, dismissed the suit, holding that the plaintiff had failed to prove his readiness and willingness. The lower appellate court, however, reversed those findings and decreed the suit. At the time of the admission of this appeal, the following substantial question of law was framed, namely, whether the lower appellate court was justified in reversing the well-reasoned findings of the trial court without adverting to the material evidence on the record. Having heard learned counsel for the parties at some length, and having carefully examined the record, this Court finds that the lower appellate court, being the final court of fact, has recorded cogent reasons for its conclusions, and has dealt with each item of the evidence led by the parties. The readiness and willingness of the plaintiff has been established not merely by his own statement, but also by the surrounding circumstances, including the part payment made and the conduct of the plaintiff in issuing the legal notice within a reasonable time. The concurrent appreciation of the documentary evidence does not disclose any perversity or misreading which would warrant interference in the exercise of the limited jurisdiction available to this Court in a second appeal. It is well settled that this Court is not to reappreciate the evidence as though it were sitting as a first appellate court, and that a finding of fact, howsoever erroneous, cannot be disturbed unless it is shown to be perverse or based on no evidence. No such infirmity having been pointed out, the substantial question of law framed is answered against the appellant. Consequently, the appeal, being devoid of merit, is dismissed, and the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court are affirmed. The parties are left to bear their own costs throughout.

title: Affidavit of the deponent
body: Affidavit of the deponent, aged about forty-two years, son of the late resident of Sector 15, Panchkula, presently working as a clerk in the establishment branch. I, the deponent above-named, do hereby solemnly affirm and declare as under. That I am the applicant in the accompanying application, and am fully conversant with the facts and circumstances of the case, and am therefore competent to swear this affidavit. That the facts stated in the accompanying application may kindly be read as an integral part of this affidavit, and are not being reproduced herein for the sake of brevity, so as to avoid unnecessary repetition. That I have not concealed any material fact from this Court, and that whatever has been stated in the application is true and correct to the best of my knowledge, and nothing material has been kept back or misstated. That the documents annexed to the application are true copies of their respective originals, the originals whereof are in my possession and shall be produced before this Court as and when so directed. That I have not filed any other application or petition, either before this Court or before any other court or authority, seeking the same or a similar relief, and that no such matter is pending anywhere. That the present application has been filed bona fide and in the interest of justice, and not with any intention to delay the proceedings or to cause any prejudice to the opposite party. That I undertake to abide by such orders and directions as this Court may deem fit to pass in the matter, and to render such assistance to the Court as may be required for the just adjudication of the controversy. That the deponent craves the leave of this Court to place on the record such further documents and facts as may become necessary during the course of the hearing, and to amend or supplement the averments made herein, if the occasion so arises. Verification. Verified at Chandigarh, on this the seventh day of September, two thousand and twenty-six, that the contents of the above affidavit are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief, that no part thereof is false, and that nothing material has been concealed therefrom. The contents have been read over and explained to me in the vernacular, which I have understood, and I have signed this affidavit in token of the correctness thereof. The deponent has been identified by the counsel appearing in the matter, who is personally known to the deponent, and whose signatures are appended below in the presence of the attesting officer. I make this solemn affirmation, believing the same to be true, and knowing that, if the statements made herein are found to be false, I shall be liable to be proceeded against in accordance with law.

title: Office note — forwarding for orders
body: Note for the kind consideration and orders of the competent authority, submitted through the proper channel. The matter relates to the representation dated the twenty-third of August, 2026, received from an official of the ministerial establishment, wherein he has requested that the period spent by him on deputation be counted towards the qualifying service for the purposes of the grant of the next higher pay scale under the assured career progression scheme. The relevant record has been examined in this branch, and the position is placed below for the perusal of the competent authority. The official concerned joined the service on the eleventh of June, 2011, and was sent on deputation to a subordinate office on the second of January, 2018, from which deputation he stood reverted on the thirtieth of September, 2021. As per the instructions on the subject, the period spent on deputation to an equivalent post is ordinarily to be counted towards the qualifying service, provided that the deputation was sanctioned by the competent authority and the requisite contributions, if any, stand recovered. On a scrutiny of the service book, it is found that the deputation was duly sanctioned vide the order noted in the margin, and that there is no adverse entry on the record which would disentitle the official to the benefit claimed. It is, however, observed that the pension contribution in respect of a part of the deputation period is yet to be reconciled with the accounts branch, and a reference in this regard is being processed separately. In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that the case appears to be covered by the instructions on the subject, and that the benefit sought may be admissible, subject to the reconciliation of the contribution referred to above. The draft of the sanction order, if approved, is placed on the flag for signatures. It is further submitted, for the information of the competent authority, that a similar representation from another official is under examination in this branch, and that a consolidated position in respect of all such cases shall be put up in due course, so as to ensure uniformity in the treatment of these matters. The file is, accordingly, submitted for such orders as the competent authority may be pleased to pass. Should the authority so desire, the dealing hand may be directed to obtain the reconciliation from the accounts branch before the sanction is issued, so that the order, when passed, is complete in all respects and does not require any subsequent amendment. Submitted, please, for orders. Put up on the noting side after the orders have been obtained, for the issuance of the necessary communication to the official concerned.

title: Notification — computer proficiency test
body: It is notified for the information of all the candidates who have qualified in the written examination for the post of Clerk that the computer proficiency test, which is the qualifying practical stage of the recruitment, shall be conducted in accordance with the schedule and the criteria set out hereunder. The candidates are advised to read the following instructions carefully, and to note that any deviation from the instructions may render a candidate liable to have his candidature cancelled. The computer proficiency test shall consist of two papers, namely, a test of English typing and a practical test in the use of a spreadsheet, and both the papers shall be of a qualifying nature only, the marks whereof shall not be added to the marks obtained in the written examination for the purpose of preparing the final merit list. In the typing test, each candidate shall be required to reproduce, within the time allowed, a printed passage handed over to him in the examination hall, and the speed shall be computed after making the deductions prescribed for the mistakes committed, the candidate being required to attain the minimum speed notified for the post. In the spreadsheet test, each candidate shall be required to enter the data supplied to him, to apply the formulae indicated in the question paper, to prepare the chart called for, and to save the work under the name specified, the whole of the exercise being marked out of the total prescribed, with a separate minimum for qualifying. The candidates shall report at the examination centre at the time indicated in their admit cards, which shall be an hour before the commencement of the session, and no candidate shall be permitted to enter the hall after the session has begun. The candidates shall bring with them the admit card and one original photo identity document, and shall not carry any mobile telephone, calculator, printed matter or writing material into the examination hall, all such articles being liable to be deposited outside the hall at the risk of the candidate. The machines and the software installed at the centre shall be provided by the commission, and the candidates shall satisfy themselves, at the commencement of the session, that the machine allotted to them is functioning properly, any defect being reported to the invigilator forthwith. The candidates are warned that the use of any unfair means, or the causing of any disturbance in the hall, shall be viewed seriously, and shall entail such action as the commission may deem fit, including the cancellation of the candidature and debarment from future examinations. The result of the computer proficiency test shall be published on the official web portal in due course, and no separate intimation shall be sent to any candidate. The candidates are advised to keep visiting the portal for further information. Issued by order of the commission for general information and strict compliance.

title: Order — regular bail (Bathinda)
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 5618 of 2025. The petitioner, Poonam Devi, through counsel, seeks the grant of regular bail in a case registered under Sections 457, 467, 379 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, at Police Station Civil Lines, Patiala. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has remained in custody for 3 months and eleventh days, that the investigation stands concluded, and that the challan was presented before the trial court on the tenth of January, 2021. It is urged that the recovery, if any, has already been effected, that no purpose would be served by a further detention, and that the petitioner is neither a previous convict nor involved in any other case of a like nature. The learned State counsel opposes the prayer and contends that the allegations are grave and that the trial is likely to be prolonged on account of the number of prosecution witnesses cited in the report under Section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the custody certificate, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has made out a case for the concession of bail. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the petition is allowed. The petitioner is ordered to be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds and one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court or the Duty Magistrate concerned. It is, however, made clear that the petitioner shall join the investigation as and when required and shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution evidence or influence any witness acquainted with the facts of the case. The application stands disposed of accordingly, and a copy of this order be sent to the trial court for information and compliance.

title: Order — anticipatory bail (Sirsa)
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Criminal Miscellaneous Application (Anticipatory Bail) No. 1872 of 2026. The petitioner, Balwinder Singh, apprehending arrest in a first information report registered under Sections 420 and 379 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, at Police Station City Kotwali, Amritsar, prays for the grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Learned counsel submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated on account of a civil dispute over the boundary of agricultural land, that the parties are closely related, and that the report was lodged after an unexplained delay of several days. It is further submitted that the petitioner is a permanent resident of the area, is not a flight risk, and is prepared to join the investigation on such date and at such time as this Court may direct. The learned State counsel, on instructions, submits that custodial interrogation would be required for the recovery of the documents said to have been fabricated. Considering the nature of the accusation and the material placed on the record, and without commenting upon the merits, this Court deems it appropriate to extend the concession of anticipatory bail on conditions. In the event of arrest, the petitioner shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and one surety to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer, subject to the conditions enumerated in Section 438(2) of the Code. The petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation as and when required, shall not leave the country without the prior permission of the Court, and shall not directly or indirectly hold out any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case. The petition is disposed of in the above terms on the fifth of September, 2023.

title: Order — interim injunction (Faridabad)
body: In the Court of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Faridabad. Civil Suit No. 7386 of 2025, titled Devinder Singh versus Manjit Kaur and others. This order shall dispose of the application filed by the plaintiff under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for the grant of an ad interim injunction. The plaintiff seeks to restrain the defendants from raising any construction over, or alienating in any manner, the suit property fully described in the head-note of the plaint, till the final decision of the suit. Learned counsel for the plaintiff contends that the plaintiff is in settled possession of the suit property, that a prima facie case is made out, and that the balance of convenience lies in favour of the plaintiff. It is argued that if the injunction is declined, the plaintiff would suffer an irreparable loss which cannot be compensated in terms of money. Learned counsel for the defendants, who has put in appearance and accepted notice, opposes the application and submits that the plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands. Having considered the rival submissions and the documents appended with the plaint, this Court is satisfied that the plaintiff has made out a prima facie case for the grant of an interim direction. Accordingly, the parties are directed to maintain the status quo, as regards the nature and possession of the suit property, till the next date of hearing. Notice of the application be issued to the remaining defendants for the sixth of January, 2025, on the plaintiff taking steps within three days.

title: Summons to the defendant (Karnal)

title: Execution notice to judgment-debtor (Jind)
body: In the Court of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Jind. Execution Application No. 5195 of 2025 in Civil Suit No. 5611 of undefined. Notice under Order XXI Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to the judgment-debtor to show cause against execution. The decree-holder, Santosh Bala, has applied for the execution of the decree dated the twentieth of October, 2025, passed in the above-noted suit, by which a sum was found due and payable by the judgment-debtor, Rajwinder Kaur. Whereas more than two years have elapsed between the date of the decree and the present application, notice is hereby issued to the judgment-debtor to appear and show cause, if any, why the decree should not be executed against him. The judgment-debtor is called upon to appear in this Court on the twenty-first of July, 2024 and to satisfy the decree, failing which the Court shall proceed to execute the decree in accordance with the mode prayed for by the decree-holder. It is open to the judgment-debtor to raise such objection to the executability of the decree as may be available to him in law, provided the same is raised on the first date of hearing and is supported by an affidavit. The decree-holder shall file the requisite process fee and furnish the correct and complete address of the judgment-debtor within a period of five days from today, so that service may be effected without avoidable delay. In case the judgment-debtor neither appears nor causes an appearance to be entered on his behalf, the notice shall be deemed to have been duly served, and the application shall be taken up for further orders in his absence.

title: Judgment — regular second appeal
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Regular Second Appeal No. 780 of 2021, Naresh Kumar versus Santosh Bala. The present appeal, under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, is directed against the judgment and decree passed by the learned first appellate court, whereby the appeal of the present appellant was dismissed and the decree of the trial court was affirmed. Briefly, the plaintiff had instituted a suit for a declaration to the effect that he was the owner in possession of the land in dispute, and for a consequential relief of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering in his possession. The trial court, on an appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, decreed the suit; the first appellate court, on a reappraisal of the same evidence, recorded a concurrent finding of fact against the defendants. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the courts below have misread the revenue record and have failed to draw the correct inference from the entries in the jamabandi. Having heard learned counsel and having perused the record, this Court finds that the findings recorded by the two courts below are findings of fact, arrived at on a proper appreciation of the evidence. It is settled that, in a second appeal, this Court would not interfere with concurrent findings of fact unless the same are shown to be perverse or based on no evidence. No substantial question of law, such as would warrant admission of the appeal, arises for consideration. In the result, the appeal is found to be without merit and is hereby dismissed, leaving the parties to bear their own costs. The judgment was pronounced in open court on the first of June, 2024.

title: Order — writ petition (mandamus)
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Civil Writ Petition No. 4542 of 2021, Simran Jeet Kaur versus State of Haryana and others. The petitioner has invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India, seeking the issuance of a writ in the nature of mandamus. The grievance of the petitioner is that, despite her selection and the recommendation of the selection committee, the order of appointment has been withheld without the communication of any reason. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the action of the respondents is arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution, and that similarly situated persons have already been issued their letters of appointment. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, seeks time to file a reply and states that the matter is under active consideration of the Deputy Commissioner. Having heard learned counsel for the parties at the motion stage, this Court is of the view that the respondents ought to take a decision, one way or the other, within a fixed time-frame. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits, the respondents are directed to consider and decide the representation of the petitioner, by a speaking order, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order. The petitioner is granted liberty to place a copy of the representation, along with the relevant documents, before the competent authority within two weeks. The petition is disposed of in these terms on the twenty-first of December, 2026. A copy of the order be given dasti under the signatures of the Bench Secretary.

title: Order — condonation of delay (Fatehabad)
body: In the Court of the District Judge, Fatehabad. Civil Miscellaneous Application No. 6752 of 2021 for condonation of delay. By this application, filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the applicant, Om Parkash, prays for the condonation of a delay of 169 days in the filing of the accompanying appeal. It is averred that the delay was neither intentional nor deliberate, but occurred on account of the prolonged illness of the applicant, who was confined to bed during the material period, as is evident from the medical record annexed with the application. It is further averred that the applicant came to know of the impugned judgment only when the certified copy was received by his counsel, and that the appeal was filed with due promptitude thereafter. Learned counsel for the respondent opposes the application and contends that the explanation offered is vague and that each day's delay has not been separately accounted for. Having considered the averments made in the application, the reply thereto, and the settled principle that the expression sufficient cause is to receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice, this Court is inclined to take a lenient view. It is well established that the refusal to condone the delay can result in a meritorious matter being thrown out at the very threshold, thereby defeating the cause of justice. Accordingly, and subject to payment of costs, the delay in the filing of the appeal is condoned. The application is allowed and the appeal be registered and listed for admission on the twenty-fourth of December, 2026.

title: Office note — the repair of the office air-conditioning
body: Office Note. Subject: Submission of the repair of the office air-conditioning for the orders of the competent authority. Kindly refer to the note recorded on the pre-page and to the connected papers flagged for ready reference at flags A to C. The matter has been examined in the light of the standing instructions on the subject, and the relevant provisions have been extracted and placed below for the convenience of perusal. As would be seen from the record, the proposal has been moved by the branch concerned after obtaining the preliminary comments of the Section Officer, and the requisite budgetary provision is available under the appropriate head of account. It is respectfully submitted that the proposal appears to be in order and does not involve any deviation from the prescribed procedure or from the financial powers delegated to this office. title: Judgment — regular second appeal
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Regular Second Appeal No. 4808 of 2025, Kamlesh Kumari versus Manjit Kaur. The present appeal, under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, is directed against the judgment and decree passed by the learned first appellate court, whereby the appeal of the present appellant was dismissed and the decree of the trial court was affirmed. Briefly, the plaintiff had instituted a suit for a declaration to the effect that he was the owner in possession of the land in dispute, and for a consequential relief of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering in his possession. The trial court, on an appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, decreed the suit; the first appellate court, on a reappraisal of the same evidence, recorded a concurrent finding of fact against the defendants. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the courts below have misread the revenue record and have failed to draw the correct inference from the entries in the jamabandi. Having heard learned counsel and having perused the record, this Court finds that the findings recorded by the two courts below are findings of fact, arrived at on a proper appreciation of the evidence. It is settled that, in a second appeal, this Court would not interfere with concurrent findings of fact unless the same are shown to be perverse or based on no evidence. No substantial question of law, such as would warrant admission of the appeal, arises for consideration. In the result, the appeal is found to be without merit and is hereby dismissed, leaving the parties to bear their own costs. The judgment was pronounced in open court on the twenty-fifth of April, 2025.

title: Order — writ petition (mandamus)

title: Order — condonation of delay (Patiala)
body: In the Court of the District Judge, Patiala. Civil Miscellaneous Application No. 4931 of 2020 for condonation of delay. By this application, filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the applicant, Ram Avtar, prays for the condonation of a delay of 137 days in the filing of the accompanying appeal. It is averred that the delay was neither intentional nor deliberate, but occurred on account of the prolonged illness of the applicant, who was confined to bed during the material period, as is evident from the medical record annexed with the application. It is further averred that the applicant came to know of the impugned judgment only when the certified copy was received by his counsel, and that the appeal was filed with due promptitude thereafter. Learned counsel for the respondent opposes the application and contends that the explanation offered is vague and that each day's delay has not been separately accounted for. Having considered the averments made in the application, the reply thereto, and the settled principle that the expression sufficient cause is to receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice, this Court is inclined to take a lenient view. It is well established that the refusal to condone the delay can result in a meritorious matter being thrown out at the very threshold, thereby defeating the cause of justice. Accordingly, and subject to payment of costs, the delay in the filing of the appeal is condoned. The application is allowed and the appeal be registered and listed for admission on the eighth of March, 2026.

body: In the Court of the District Judge, Hisar. Civil Miscellaneous Application No. 1416 of 2019 for condonation of delay. The petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation as and when required, shall not leave the country without the prior permission of the Court, and shall not directly or indirectly hold out any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case. title: Proclamation under Section 82 (Rohtak)
body: In the Court of the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Rewari. Proclamation requiring the appearance of a person accused, under Section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Whereas complaint has been made before this Court that Devinder Singh has committed, or is suspected to have committed, an offence punishable under Sections 468 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, in a case registered at Police Station Model Town, Rohtak; And whereas it has been returned to a warrant of arrest thereupon issued that the said Devinder Singh cannot be found, and this Court has reason to believe that the said person has absconded, or is concealing himself to avoid the service of the said warrant; Proclamation is hereby made that the said Devinder Singh is required to appear before this Court, to answer the said complaint, on the sixteenth of December, 2020, being a date not less than thirty days from the date of the publication of this proclamation. A copy of this proclamation shall be publicly read in some conspicuous place of the town or village in which the said person ordinarily resides, and shall be affixed to some conspicuous part of the house in which he ordinarily resides. A further copy shall be affixed to some conspicuous part of the court-house, and, if the Court so directs, may be published in a daily newspaper circulating in the place in which the said person ordinarily resides. Take notice that, in the event of a failure to appear within the time so specified, the property, movable and immovable, belonging to the said person shall be liable to attachment in accordance with law. Given under my hand and the seal of the Court on the fifteenth of March, 2024. The station house officer concerned shall ensure the due publication of this proclamation and shall submit a report of compliance to this Court.

title: Daily cause list (Panipat)
body: In the Court of the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Panipat. Daily cause list for the twenty-eighth of March, 2019, to be read subject to the orders of the Court. Notice is hereby given to the members of the Bar and to the litigant public that the cases mentioned in the list appended below shall be taken up on the date noted above, in the order in which they are entered. The list contains a total of 22 cases, comprising matters listed for arguments, for evidence, for the framing of issues, and for miscellaneous orders, which shall be called out in three separate parts. In the first part, the cases fixed for the pronouncement of orders and for the framing of charge shall be taken up, immediately after the assembly of the Court in the forenoon. In the second part, the cases fixed for the recording of the statements of witnesses shall be taken up, and the parties are directed to keep their witnesses present, in the Court, well in time. In the third part, the cases fixed for arguments shall be taken up, and learned counsel are requested to be ready with the relevant record and the precedents on which they propose to place reliance. An adjournment shall not be granted as a matter of course, and a party seeking an adjournment shall file an application, supported by an affidavit, setting out the ground on which the adjournment is prayed for. The Reader of the Court shall ensure that the cases are entered in the correct order, that the connected files are placed on the table before the commencement of the day's work, and that any correction in the list is duly notified on the notice board.

title: Order — regular bail (Mohali)
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 337 of 2021. The petitioner, Usha Rani, through counsel, seeks the grant of regular bail in a case registered under Sections 457, 498-A, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, at Police Station Civil Lines, Patiala. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has remained in custody for 10 months and twenty-third days, that the investigation stands concluded, and that the challan was presented before the trial court on the twentieth of June, 2023. It is urged that the recovery, if any, has already been effected, that no purpose would be served by a further detention, and that the petitioner is neither a previous convict nor involved in any other case of a like nature. The learned State counsel opposes the prayer and contends that the allegations are grave and that the trial is likely to be prolonged on account of the number of prosecution witnesses cited in the report under Section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the custody certificate, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has made out a case for the concession of bail. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the petition is allowed. The petitioner is ordered to be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds and one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court or the Duty Magistrate concerned. It is, however, made clear that the petitioner shall join the investigation as and when required and shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution evidence or influence any witness acquainted with the facts of the case. The application stands disposed of accordingly, and a copy of this order be sent to the trial court for information and compliance.

title: Order — anticipatory bail (Chandigarh)
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Criminal Miscellaneous Application (Anticipatory Bail) No. 5422 of 2026. The petitioner, Mohan Lal, apprehending arrest in a first information report registered under Sections 341 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, at Police Station Model Town, Rohtak, prays for the grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Learned counsel submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated on account of a civil dispute over the boundary of agricultural land, that the parties are closely related, and that the report was lodged after an unexplained delay of several days. It is further submitted that the petitioner is a permanent resident of the area, is not a flight risk, and is prepared to join the investigation on such date and at such time as this Court may direct. The learned State counsel, on instructions, submits that custodial interrogation would be required for the recovery of the documents said to have been fabricated. Considering the nature of the accusation and the material placed on the record, and without commenting upon the merits, this Court deems it appropriate to extend the concession of anticipatory bail on conditions. In the event of arrest, the petitioner shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and one surety to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer, subject to the conditions enumerated in Section 438(2) of the Code. The petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation as and when required, shall not leave the country without the prior permission of the Court, and shall not directly or indirectly hold out any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case. The petition is disposed of in the above terms on the nineteenth of August, 2021.

title: Order — interim injunction (Panchkula)
body: In the Court of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Panchkula. Civil Suit No. 296 of 2024, titled Harpreet Kaur versus Krishan Chand and others. This order shall dispose of the application filed by the plaintiff under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for the grant of an ad interim injunction. The plaintiff seeks to restrain the defendants from raising any construction over, or alienating in any manner, the suit property fully described in the head-note of the plaint, till the final decision of the suit. Learned counsel for the plaintiff contends that the plaintiff is in settled possession of the suit property, that a prima facie case is made out, and that the balance of convenience lies in favour of the plaintiff. It is argued that if the injunction is declined, the plaintiff would suffer an irreparable loss which cannot be compensated in terms of money. Learned counsel for the defendants, who has put in appearance and accepted notice, opposes the application and submits that the plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands. Having considered the rival submissions and the documents appended with the plaint, this Court is satisfied that the plaintiff has made out a prima facie case for the grant of an interim direction. Accordingly, the parties are directed to maintain the status quo, as regards the nature and possession of the suit property, till the next date of hearing. Notice of the application be issued to the remaining defendants for the twenty-seventh of March, 2023, on the plaintiff taking steps within three days.

title: Summons to the defendant (Yamunanagar)
body: In the Court of the Civil Judge (Junior Division), Yamunanagar. Summons to the defendant under Order V Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Civil Suit No. 3541 of 2025, Poonam Devi versus Satpal Sharma, for recovery and permanent injunction. To Satpal Sharma, resident of the district of Yamunanagar. Whereas the above-named plaintiff has instituted a suit against you upon the cause of action set out in the plaint, you are hereby summoned to appear in this Court in person, or by a pleader duly instructed and able to answer all material questions relating to the suit. You are required to appear on the thirteenth of December, 2026 at ten of the clock in the forenoon, to answer the claim of the plaintiff, and a copy of the plaint is delivered herewith. Take notice that, in default of your appearance on the day so fixed, the suit will be heard and determined in your absence, in accordance with law. You are further directed to produce, on the said date, all documents upon which you intend to rely in support of your defence, and to bring with you, or send by your pleader, any documents which are in your possession or power and which you are required to produce. Should you admit the claim, you may deposit the amount so admitted in this Court, together with the costs of the suit, whereupon further proceedings against you may be stayed to that extent. Given under my hand and the seal of the Court on the twenty-eighth of September, 2022. The process fee and the requisites for service having been filed, the office shall ensure that service is effected sufficiently in advance of the date so appointed.

title: Execution notice to judgment-debtor (Chandigarh)
body: In the Court of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Chandigarh. Execution Application No. 7050 of 2023 in Civil Suit No. 3240 of undefined. Notice under Order XXI Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to the judgment-debtor to show cause against execution. The decree-holder, Sunita Rani, has applied for the execution of the decree dated the twenty-sixth of November, 2022, passed in the above-noted suit, by which a sum was found due and payable by the judgment-debtor, Jagtar Singh. Whereas more than two years have elapsed between the date of the decree and the present application, notice is hereby issued to the judgment-debtor to appear and show cause, if any, why the decree should not be executed against him. The judgment-debtor is called upon to appear in this Court on the thirteenth of November, 2025 and to satisfy the decree, failing which the Court shall proceed to execute the decree in accordance with the mode prayed for by the decree-holder. It is open to the judgment-debtor to raise such objection to the executability of the decree as may be available to him in law, provided the same is raised on the first date of hearing and is supported by an affidavit. The decree-holder shall file the requisite process fee and furnish the correct and complete address of the judgment-debtor within a period of five days from today, so that service may be effected without avoidable delay. In case the judgment-debtor neither appears nor causes an appearance to be entered on his behalf, the notice shall be deemed to have been duly served, and the application shall be taken up for further orders in his absence.

title: Judgment — regular second appeal
body: In the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Regular Second Appeal No. 2045 of 2025, Simran Jeet Kaur versus Krishan Chand. The present appeal, under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, is directed against the judgment and decree passed by the learned first appellate court, whereby the appeal of the present appellant was dismissed and the decree of the trial court was affirmed. Briefly, the plaintiff had instituted a suit for a declaration to the effect that he was the owner in possession of the land in dispute, and for a consequential relief of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering in his possession. The trial court, on an appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, decreed the suit; the first appellate court, on a reappraisal of the same evidence, recorded a concurrent finding of fact against the defendants. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the courts below have misread the revenue record and have failed to draw the correct inference from the entries in the jamabandi. Having heard learned counsel and having perused the record, this Court finds that the findings recorded by the two courts below are findings of fact, arrived at on a proper appreciation of the evidence. It is settled that, in a second appeal, this Court would not interfere with concurrent findings of fact unless the same are shown to be perverse or based on no evidence. No substantial question of law, such as would warrant admission of the appeal, arises for consideration. In the result, the appeal is found to be without merit and is hereby dismissed, leaving the parties to bear their own costs. The judgment was pronounced in open court on the fourteenth of August, 2026.
